o: Good for Indian monsoon causing more rains

ex.1: Radiation fog increases after a WD passes (rain moistens, then clear skies and cold nights).
ex.8: Rainfall shifts with the monsoon trough: normal position along the Gangetic plains gives rain over most of India; along the foothills gives a break.
ex.11: Fair weather over Assam during the monsoon indicates a depression forming or intensifying over the head Bay.
ex.15: In July the lowest pressure (994 hPa) lies over Baluchistan/Pakistan.
ex.17: Monsoon: easterlies above 500 hPa; TEJ at 15–16 km near 13°N.
ex.18: Winter: westerlies aloft over all India (STJ at 12 km over the north).
ex.21: Winter: NW–W winds at 6 km over N India.
ex.22: Winter westerlies at 6 km on an ESE track: mainly a tailwind; the book's key gives (a) port drift.
ex.23: Kolkata → Nagpur is westbound; NW winds at 2 km come from the right → port drift (and a headwind component).
ex.26: The subtropical (mid-tropospheric) cyclone forms in the monsoon at 500–700 hPa over Gujarat/NE Arabian Sea.
